text: Ah, it's you. I knew you would come. Not hoped — knew. Strange, isn't it?
Do you remember the beacon on the hill above the Ford? Once its fire could be seen from every window. And its warm wind drove the smoke away.

first2.text: Then came the decree: light, they said, brings misfortune. We put out the beacon. Locked our doors. And waited for the darkness to leave on its own.

first3.text: It didn't. Darkness never leaves on its own — I understood that too late. It only teaches you to wait. And waiting without hope… that is how people turn into shades.

first3b.text: We obeyed. Obeying is easier than deciding. I was the elder — and I chose to stay silent. That is my fault, and I won't hide it.

text: Here. My father kept this lantern for forty winters. The last fire left in the Ford. I want you to have it.
The beacon is on the hill, the road starts at the square. Keep to the light. The oil won't last long — be sparing.

choices.text: I'm old, Oldrich. My legs aren't what they were.

why_old.text: Patience walks slowly. But it walks the farthest. You went out every evening and lit the street lamps — twenty years, one step at a time.

why_me.text: Because you alone kept going out at dusk to light the lamps — even when the decree forbade it, even when no one was left to see them. I watched from my window. I was ashamed. And warmed.

promise.text: Don't promise. Just go. Promises are heavy, and you still have a lantern to carry.

go.text: Shades fear fire. Raise the lantern high and they will draw back. But what they fear most is someone who doesn't give up. Look in on Mara at the teahouse — she always has a little oil. And on Borta: he is a master, though he grumbles.

text: The beacon is waiting. It has waited a long time — it can wait a little more while you catch your breath.
If your oil runs low — go to Mara. If the lantern is weak — to Borta. And if you're afraid… then you're alive. That's good too.
Do you hear that? A rooster… A rooster is crowing. I'd forgotten what an awful voice they have. The most beautiful sound in the world.
Look at the people. They're standing on their doorsteps, looking up. They forgot how — and now they remember.

choices.text: I was afraid I wouldn't make it.

after_fear.text: And yet you did. Fear walks beside everyone who walks. It never leaves — it just falls behind, if you don't stop.

after2.text: The other beacons are farther. The nearest is in the Whispering Wood, to the north — the trail starts behind the houses. Vale the herbalist lives there; stubborn, but kind. Then the mire, the mountains. And the last one is in the castle ruins, where the king lives. Don't hurry. But don't stop.

later.text: Today two people quarrelled at the well over whose turn it was for water. They argued — and their eyes were happy. Go on, lamplighter. We'll manage here.
